extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining, requiring, and administering restriction (election/division) practice and handling double patenting issues in U.S. national patent applications under 35 U.S.C. 121 and related 37 CFR rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory basis for restriction/double patenting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis for restriction and double patenting practices is found in 35 U.S.C. 121 (Divisional applications) and in the implementing rules such as 37 CFR 1.141 (Different inventions in one national application) and 37 CFR 1.142 (Requirement for restriction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and conform to the language of 35 U.S.C. 121 and 37 CFR 1.141/1.142 when making restriction or division decisions; consult PCT-related MPEP sections (e.g., Chapter 1800) for international-stage considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'independent' invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent means not dependent or unrelated; there is no disclosed relationship between the two or more inventions claimed (i.e., they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a process and an apparatus incapable of being used in practicing the process are independent inventions. See MPEP § 806.06 and § 808.01 for further examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'distinct' invention (related but distinct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related inventions are distinct if the inventions as claimed are not connected in at least one of design, operation, or effect (e.g., can be made by, or used in, a materially different process) and wherein at least one invention is patentable (novel and nonobvious) over the other (though they may each be unpatentable over the prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related examples include combination and subcombination, process and apparatus for its practice, process and product made. When related in two different ways, applicable distinctness criteria for each relation must be demonstrated (see MPEP § 806.05(c) and § 806.05(j)). Read case law carefully because 'independent' and 'distinct' have varied usage in decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is the practice of requiring an applicant to elect a single claimed invention (e.g., a combination or subcombination invention, a product or process invention, a species within a genus) for examination when two or more independent inventions and/or two or more distinct inventions are claimed in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making a restriction requirement, specify how the application is to be restricted and make the requirement complete (see form paragraph guidance in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: When restriction is proper (core two-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A restriction requirement between patentably distinct inventions is proper only if: (A) the inventions are independent or distinct as claimed; and (B) there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search and examination of all claims can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits even if they include independent or distinct inventions. Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples to support conclusions, though citation of documents is not generally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious burden prima facie showing
rubrics_metrics.description: A serious burden on the examiner may be prima facie shown by appropriate explanation of separate classification, separate status in the art, or a different field of search (as defined in MPEP § 808.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prima facie showing may be rebutted by the applicant. Examiners should articulate the nature of the burden (e.g., separate art areas or search strategies) when asserting serious burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination obligation when no serious burden
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search and examination of all the claims in an application can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits even though they include independent or distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not require restriction merely because multiple inventions are claimed if the examiner can fully search and examine all claims without serious burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide reasons/examples for restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples to support conclusions for restriction requirements, but need not cite documents to support the restriction requirement in most cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where plural inventions are capable of being viewed as related in two ways, both applicable criteria for distinctness must be demonstrated to support a restriction requirement. If applicant has expressly admitted obviousness between claimed inventions, restriction should not be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review/signature authority for final restriction actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an examiner with permanent full signatory authority or temporary full signatory authority may sign final Office actions containing a final requirement for restriction. An examiner with permanent partial signatory authority or temporary partial signatory authority may sign non-final Office actions containing a final requirement for restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects public interest by reducing issuance of improper restrictions that could lead to two patents for the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type claim unity and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of a Markush group ordinarily must belong to a recognized physical/chemical class or art-recognized class. For Markush groups in process or combination claims, members must be disclosed to possess at least one property in common that is mainly responsible for their function in the claimed relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity exists where Markush members (1) share a common utility, and (2) share a substantial structural feature essential to that utility. If members are few or closely related so that full search/examination can be made without serious burden, examine all members. If a Markush encompasses independent/distinct inventions, the examiner may require provisional election of a single species (use form paragraphs 8.01 or 8.02 as applicable). After election, examine the Markush claim with respect to the elected species and as necessary to determine patentability; do not extend the prior art search unnecessarily to cover all nonelected species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures after provisional election of a Markush species
rubrics_metrics.description: Following provisional election of a species in a Markush claim, the Markush claim is examined with respect to the elected species; if elected species is unallowable (anticipated/obvious), the Markush claim and claims to the elected species are rejected and nonelected species claims are held withdrawn from further consideration (subject to standard rules on finality and new grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If elected species is allowable, examination of the Markush claim will be extended as necessary. If prior art later found anticipates or renders obvious the Markush claim for a nonelected species, the Markush claim shall be rejected and nonelected species held withdrawn. Applicants may amend to exclude problematic species and reexamination will follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional application restriction fee and exceptions (37 CFR 1.129)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain 'transitional' applications pending ≥3 years as of June 8, 1995, no requirement for restriction or divisional filings shall be made or maintained after that date except where (i) the requirement was first made prior to April 8, 1995; (ii) the examiner was prevented from making a restriction prior to April 8, 1995 due to applicant actions; or (iii) the required fee for examination of each additional invention was not paid. If restriction cannot be made, applicant is notified and may elect inventions and pay the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(s), confirm a prior election and pay, or file a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of applicant actions that prevent prior restriction include abandonment and refiling, suspension of prosecution, delaying presentation of claims to multiple inventions, or combining separate applications into a later continuing application. Use form paragraph 8.41 for notification and follow fee and petition procedures in 37 CFR 1.17(s) and 1.129(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund practice for transitional applications when linking or generic claim becomes allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever divided inventions in a transitional application are rejoined because a linking claim is allowable, or whenever claims to an additional species are no longer withdrawn because they are fully embraced by an allowable generic claim, applicant should be notified that he or she may request a refund of the fee paid for that additional invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make refund notifications when the conditions described in MPEP §§ 803.03(a) and 803.03(b) are met and follow the procedural guidance and form paragraphs referenced in MPEP (e.g., §§ 821.04, 806.04(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide sequence partial waiver and reasonable number rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide sequences encoding different proteins are normally independent and distinct inventions; however, the Director has sua sponte partially waived 37 CFR 1.141 et seq. to permit a reasonable number (normally ten) of such nucleotide sequences to be claimed in a single application and examined without restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to ten independent/distinct nucleotide sequences will typically be examined in a single application without restriction; sequences patentably indistinct from selected sequences and sequences encoding the same protein are not considered independent and will be examined together. Exceptional cases may require fewer than ten. Applicants may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 for examination of additional sequences by providing evidence that the sequences do not cover independent and distinct inventions. Combinations of sequences (e.g., composition claims) are generally not subject to restriction; search order should maximize identification of an allowable sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of process claims requiring an allowable product claim
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims to a product and to a process of making and/or using that product are presented, and applicant elects the product, withdrawn process claims which depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable product claim will be considered for rejoinder. Upon rejoinder, the restriction requirement between the elected product and rejoined process(es) will be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All rejoined process claims must depend from or otherwise require all limitations of the allowable product claim. If applicant cancels all nonelected process claims before rejoinder, preserve restriction to protect 35 U.S.C. 121 rights. Amendments after final rejection or allowance are governed by applicable CFR sections (e.g., 1.116, 1.312) and rejoinder timing affects entry of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conflicting claims in plural/copending applications (37 CFR 1.78(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant contain conflicting claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required in the absence of good and sufficient reason for their retention during pendency in more than one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make complete examinations of claims in each application and enter appropriate rejections, including provisional double patenting rejections, as long as conflicting claims exist in more than one application. Use form paragraph 8.29 where conflicting claims are identical or conceded not patentably distinct. The 'provisional' double patenting rejection should continue in each application while conflicting claims exist unless it is the only rejection remaining in at least one application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional double patenting practice and interaction with restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: When restriction requirements are made and withdrawals/rejoinders occur, claims presented in continuations or divisionals that are anticipated by or include all limitations of a claim allowable in the present application may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections over the instant application's claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction requirement is withdrawn (e.g., due to rejoinder or allowance of linking/generic claim), 35 U.S.C. 121 protections no longer apply; examiners should consider provisional double patenting rejections and related MPEP sections (e.g., § 804.01). Applicants should be advised of potential double patenting consequences when rejoin/withdrawal occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and procedural requirements when making restriction/election and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specified form paragraphs (e.g., 8.01, 8.02, 8.21.04, 8.29, 8.41, 8.42, 8.43, 8.46–8.50, etc.) to set forth restriction or election requirements, notices for transitional applications, rejoin notifications, and condition-for-allowance letters involving withdrawn claims with traverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs prescribe exact wording and are to be used in the appropriate circumstances (e.g., provisional election of species in Markush claims, notification of transitional restriction status, rejoinder after allowable product claim). Follow examiner notes in MPEP for when to use each paragraph and for bracket insertions.
